title: Graviton4 ONNX Runtime thread and memory tuning ablation
hypothesis: At least one preregistered ONNX Runtime thread or memory treatment will sustain 0.62 requests/s under the unchanged 10-second p95 SLO while the current KleidiAI-enabled runtime fails, establishing at least 10.7% capacity above the accepted 0.56 requests/s boundary.
independent_variable: ORT worker-spin policy, mimalloc preload, and transparent huge-page policy
controls: same mixed workload and 10-second p95 SLO
exclusive process restart and warmup before every window
acceptance: candidate passes both 120-second screens at 0.62 requests/s
candidate improves median screen p95 by at least 5% over current
selected candidate passes five 300-second confirmations at 0.62 requests/s
current runtime fails five matched confirmations at 0.62 requests/s
warmup outputs remain byte-equivalent across variants
notes: Screening was deliberately short; only a candidate clearing the frozen screen gate received long confirmation. Neutral and failed variants remain in the evidence bundle. No threshold changed after launch. EXP-2026-016 subsequently isolated the likely contributions of THP and mimalloc, but the sustained claim in this experiment applies to the exact combined thread-memory treatment tested here.
